issues.legal_issue: A post-decree application to reduce a secured debt is available where the decree is covered by the debt-reduction scheme and the mortgaged property is an estate acquired under the relevant land-reform law, even if the decree did not charge that property.
material_facts: A decree was passed in respect of a secured debt.
The mortgaged property consisted of an estate acquired under the relevant land-reform law.
The debtors sought reduction of the decretal amount under the debt-reduction scheme.
An amendment deleted the requirement that the mortgaged property be charged under the decree and provided that the amendment operated as if it had been in force on all material dates.
The debt had not been discharged before the amendment was enacted.
issues.conclusion: The debtors were entitled to apply for reduction, and the Special Judge was required to proceed with the application under the amended scheme; the absence of a charge over the mortgaged property in the decree did not bar relief.
issues.legal_principle: The amendment's retrospective deeming clause required the amended law to be treated as having been in force on all material dates, with the statutory fiction carried through to its logical consequences. The words requiring the property to be charged under the decree were therefore treated as absent from the scheme from its commencement. The Court applied State of Bombay v. Pandurang Vinayak Chaphalkar and the principle stated in East End Dwellings Company Ltd. v. Finsbury Borough Council. The relevant conditions were that the decree be one to which the scheme applied, relate to a secured debt, and concern mortgaged property consisting of an estate acquired under the specified land-reform law; the amendment did not apply to a debt already discharged before its enactment.

rule.if: post_decree_secured_debt_reduction and covered_decree and secured_debt and acquired_estate_mortgaged_property and retrospective_amendment_applies and not debt_previously_discharged

predicates.post_decree_secured_debt_reduction: A debtor or creditor sought reduction of a secured debt after a decree had been passed.
predicates.covered_decree: The decree was one covered by the debt-reduction scheme.
predicates.secured_debt: The decree related to a debt secured by property.
predicates.acquired_estate_mortgaged_property: The mortgaged property consisted of an estate acquired under the applicable land-reform law.
predicates.retrospective_amendment_applies: An amendment removing the requirement that the property be charged under the decree was made effective for the material dates.
predicates.debt_previously_discharged: The debt had been discharged before the amendment was enacted.

issues.definition: When a covered post-decree secured-debt reduction application concerns mortgaged property consisting of an acquired estate, the retrospective amendment applies, and the debt was not previously discharged, the court must process the application.

issues.legal_issue: A High Court may revisit its earlier decision on a statutory debt-reduction application when a retrospective amendment shows that the earlier decision applied a legal rule that was not applicable on the relevant dates.
material_facts: The debtors' application for reduction had been rejected by the Special Judge, and the High Court had dismissed their challenge.
After the High Court's decision, an amendment was enacted with effect from the commencement of the debt-reduction scheme, subject to an exception for debts already discharged.
The earlier decision had relied on the requirement that the mortgaged property be charged under the decree, a requirement removed by the retrospective amendment.
The debtors applied to the High Court to revisit its decision, and the High Court set aside the rejection and remanded the matter for consideration under the amended scheme.
The statutory debt-reduction scheme conferred a right to apply notwithstanding provisions of the Code of Civil Procedure.
issues.conclusion: The High Court was entitled to grant the application and remand the matter. The retrospective amendment meant the earlier decision had applied a rule that was not the law applicable to the case, producing an error apparent on the face of the record; the substance of the application, rather than its designation as a review, was decisive.
issues.legal_principle: Under Order 47 of the Code of Civil Procedure, review is generally available for discovery of qualifying new matter or evidence, or for an error apparent on the face of the record; a subsequent change in law ordinarily does not justify review. However, this amendment was not merely a subsequent change: its deeming clause made the amended law applicable to the earlier material dates, so applying the former rule was an apparent error. The Court relied on Rajah Kotagiri Venkata Subbamma Rao v. Rajah Vellanki Venkatrama Rao concerning the limits on review for subsequent events, and on State of Bombay v. Pandurang Vinayak Chaphalkar and East End Dwellings Company Ltd. v. Finsbury Borough Council concerning the full effect of statutory fictions. Because the special statutory scheme conferred relief notwithstanding the Code, the substance of the request controlled over its form.

rule.if: high_court_reconsideration_proceeding and prior_order_applied_superseded_rule and retrospective_amendment_applies and eligible_debt_reduction_claim and not debt_previously_discharged and special_scheme_overrides_general_procedure

predicates.high_court_reconsideration_proceeding: A party asked a High Court to reconsider its earlier decision on a challenge to the rejection of a statutory debt-reduction application.
predicates.prior_order_applied_superseded_rule: The earlier decision applied a rule that the later amendment made inapplicable to the material dates.
predicates.retrospective_amendment_applies: The amendment was made effective for the dates relevant to the earlier decision.
predicates.eligible_debt_reduction_claim: The claim concerned a covered decree relating to a secured debt and mortgaged property consisting of an acquired estate.
predicates.debt_previously_discharged: The debt had been discharged before the amendment was enacted.
predicates.special_scheme_overrides_general_procedu: The special statutory scheme authorized the application notwithstanding the general procedural code.

issues.definition: When a High Court is asked to reconsider an earlier order that applied a superseded rule, a retrospective amendment applies to an eligible claim, the debt was not previously discharged, and the special scheme overrides general procedure, the High Court may reopen the order and remand for reconsideration.
